title: Missouri Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights: Rules for Selling a Rental
content:
Missouri Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights: Rules for Selling a Rental

What the official sources say

  • Within thirty days after termination of the tenancy the landlord must furnish a written itemized list of damages withheld, with the balance of the deposit. (RSMo 535.300; source)
  • If the landlord wrongfully withholds the deposit, the tenant recovers twice the amount wrongfully withheld. (RSMo 535.300; source)
  • A tenancy at will/sufferance or for less than one year, and unwritten month-to-month tenancies, terminate on one month's written notice; month-to-month ends on a periodic rent-paying date not less than one month after receipt of notice. (RSMo 441.060; source)
  • Mobile-home lot tenancies under one year: landlord notice not sooner than sixty days from the date rent next becomes due. (RSMo 441.060(2); source)
Selling in Missouri?

Get My Cash Offer →

What does Missouri landlord tenant law mean for someone selling a rental house?

It means the lease, the deposit and the way a tenancy ends all travel with the house, so you need to know where each stands before a buyer gets involved. Missouri has no single landlord-tenant code. The rules sit in Chapters 441, 534 and 535 of the Revised Statutes, and the Attorney General's office publishes a plain-language guide that points owners and renters to those chapters.

A rental that is sold keeps its tenant. The buyer steps into a house with a lease already running, a deposit already held and perhaps a month-to-month renter who can be given notice only in writing. The Attorney General's guide tells landlords to give tenants written notice when ownership passes to a new landlord, which is the first piece of paperwork to plan for on a Missouri sale.

Owners who sell to a buyer that wants the property vacant face a different job. Under the statutes you cannot simply ask a tenant to leave on the closing date. The notice period, the type of tenancy and the court process all have to be respected, and the sections below walk through each in turn.

How much security deposit can a Missouri landlord hold?

A landlord may not demand or receive more than two months of rent as a security deposit. Under RSMo 535.300, the money must sit in an insured bank, credit union or similar depository, and any interest it earns belongs to the landlord. A deposit labeled as a pet deposit falls outside the statutory definition.

When the tenancy ends, the landlord has thirty days to do one of two things: return the full deposit, or mail the tenant an itemized written list of the damages withheld together with whatever balance remains. Mailing to the tenant's last known address counts as compliance. Before deducting anything, the landlord must give the tenant reasonable written notice of a move-out inspection time, and the tenant may attend.

The allowed deductions are narrow:

  • unpaid rent owed under the rental agreement;
  • restoring the unit to its starting condition, with ordinary wear and tear excluded;
  • carpet cleaning, only if the lease set that charge in advance and warned the tenant, with a receipt for the actual cost due within thirty days;
  • actual losses from a tenant who left without giving adequate notice, provided the landlord tried to limit those losses.

A landlord who wrongfully keeps any part of the deposit owes the tenant twice the amount withheld. For an owner about to sell, that doubling is the reason to settle the deposit ledger cleanly. Ask your closing agent how the deposit will be handled between you and the buyer, and put the answer in writing.

How does a Missouri tenancy end, and how much notice is required?

A tenancy with no written, signed lease is treated as month to month, and either side can end it with one month of written notice. RSMo 441.060 says the termination date must fall on a periodic rent-paying date at least one month after the notice is received. The Attorney General's guide adds that oral notice from either party is not valid, and that a lease running a year or longer must be written and signed.

A written lease ends on the date it names, and neither side owes the other notice unless the lease has an automatic renewal clause. The guide warns that a tenant who stays past the end date without a written agreement can be charged double rent. A tenant who sublets without the landlord's approval can also face double rent.

Three other rules can matter on a sale:

  • Mobile home lot tenancies shorter than a year need sixty days of landlord notice, counted from the date the next rent payment comes due.
  • An occupancy limit of two people per bedroom is presumed reasonable, though it does not apply to a child born to the tenants during the lease.
  • An active-duty service member may end a lease on 15 days' notice after a permanent change of station, certain long orders, discharge, or an order to government quarters, and is entitled to a full deposit refund if the other lease terms were met.

Can a Missouri landlord remove a tenant without a court order?

No. The Attorney General's guide states that a landlord may not evict a tenant without a court order. Grounds for starting a case include unpaid rent, property damage, a lease violation, staying past the end of the term, drug-related activity, illegal gambling and allowing a person the landlord previously excluded to live there. The tenant receives notice of the lawsuit and a chance to be heard before any removal.

After a judgment, RSMo 441.060 sets a self-help path with strict conditions. If the officer holding the writ has not delivered possession within seven days, the landlord has sixty days from the judgment to enter without breaching the peace, in the presence of a local law enforcement officer who has been shown the judgment and execution order and acknowledges that in writing. That acknowledgment must be filed with the court within five days after possession is taken.

Shutting off water, power or gas to push a tenant out is a different matter. The guide says a landlord who willfully interrupts utility service commits forcible entry unless the interruption is for health and safety reasons. If a rental is lost to foreclosure, RSMo 534.030 gives a residential occupant a notice from the new owner and at least ten business days before any possession suit can start.

What repair rights do Missouri tenants have?

Missouri tenants have very little room to withhold rent. The Attorney General's guide says that in most circumstances a tenant has no right to hold back payment, and that doing so can lead to eviction. The one narrow exception is repair and deduct under RSMo 441.234.

That section applies only to a tenant who has lived in the unit six consecutive months, has paid all rent and charges, and has not received an uncured written lease or house rule violation notice. The condition must hurt habitability, sanitation or security and violate a local housing or building code. The repair cost must be under $300 or half of the periodic rent, whichever is greater, and never more than one month's rent.

The tenant notifies the landlord, waits fourteen days, and then may have the work done and deduct the documented cost. If the landlord disputes the need in writing, the tenant needs a written certification from the local government that the code is violated before doing the work. Total deductions cannot exceed one month's rent in any twelve months, and a lease cannot waive these rights. Owners who plan to sell should clear any open repair request first, because a pending code issue gives a buyer's inspector something to cite.

What are the key Missouri landlord tenant numbers at a glance?

Missouri rental rules and where each one is written
TopicRuleSource
Security deposit capTwo months of rentRSMo 535.300
Deposit return30 days after the tenancy ends, with an itemized list if any is keptRSMo 535.300
Penalty for wrongful withholdingTwice the amount withheldRSMo 535.300
Month-to-month noticeOne month, in writingRSMo 441.060
Mobile home lot, lease under one year60 days from the next rent due dateRSMo 441.060
Repair and deductUnder $300 or half of one month, whichever is greater; 14 days after written noticeRSMo 441.234
Foreclosed rental occupantAt least 10 business days after the new owner's noticeRSMo 534.030

What should an owner do before selling a Missouri rental?

Start by pulling the signed lease, the deposit record and any written notices already sent to the tenant. Then match the end date of the tenancy against your target closing date. A month-to-month tenant who has not been given a proper written notice can stay, so a buyer who wants an empty house needs the notice served early enough to land on a rent-paying date.

  • Confirm whether the deposit sits in an insured account and what it totals.
  • Send the tenant written notice of the ownership change, as the Attorney General's guide recommends.
  • Close out any open repair request and keep the receipts.
  • Hold an inspection for move-out only after giving the tenant reasonable written notice of the time.
  • Keep fair housing rules in mind when talking with prospective buyers or tenants: the guide lists race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status and national origin as protected, and points to the Missouri Human Rights Commission at 877-781-4236 for complaints.

More questions about Missouri Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights

Does a tenant's lease survive the sale of a Missouri rental house?

The lease stays in place unless it ends by its own terms or by proper notice. Missouri does not give a seller a way to cancel a lease because a sale is coming. The Attorney General's guide advises landlords to give the tenants written notice when ownership changes hands, so plan on sending that letter at or before closing.

What is the most a Missouri landlord can charge as a deposit?

Two months of rent is the ceiling under RSMo 535.300. Money a tenant pays specifically as a pet deposit is outside the statutory definition of a security deposit, so the cap and the thirty-day return clock apply to the general deposit.

Can I give a month-to-month tenant a verbal notice to move?

No. The Attorney General's guide states that oral notice from either party is not valid. A month-to-month tenancy ends only through a written notice that names a rent-paying date at least one month after the other side receives it.

Can I change the locks or cut the utilities to speed up a sale?

No. A landlord needs a court order to evict, and the Attorney General's guide says willfully interrupting water, electricity or gas is forcible entry unless done for health and safety. After a judgment, entry is allowed only under the conditions in RSMo 441.060, including a law enforcement officer's written acknowledgment.

Can a tenant deduct repair costs from rent?

Only in a narrow case. The tenant must have lived there six months, be current on rent, face a code-violating condition that affects habitability, sanitation or security, and give the landlord fourteen days after written notice. The deduction is capped by RSMo 441.234 at $300 or half of the periodic rent, whichever is greater, and never over one month's rent.

Missouri Eviction Notice Rules: Notice Types, Days and Selling the House

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Missouri Eviction Notice Rules sale

Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • If rent is not paid as agreed, the landlord may dispossess the tenant and subtenants and recover possession in the manner provided in chapter 535. (RSMo 535.010; source)
Selling in Missouri?
We buy Missouri houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What notice does a Missouri landlord have to give before an eviction?

It depends on why the landlord wants the tenant out. A landlord who is owed rent can skip the termination notice and go straight to court after demanding payment, while a landlord ending a tenancy with no rent default must give a written notice that runs one month. Missouri sets these two tracks in RSMo 535.020 and RSMo 441.060.

For a seller with a rented house, this split decides the schedule. If the tenant is behind, the clock starts with a rent demand and a filing. If the tenant is current and simply has to leave before closing, the clock starts with a written notice.

Is a rent demand required before a nonpayment case starts?

Yes. Under RSMo 535.020 the rent must have come due, the landlord or the landlord's agent must have demanded it from the tenant or whoever occupies the home, and it must remain unpaid. The landlord then signs an affidavit for an associate circuit judge that lists the rental terms, the amount actually due, the demand, and a description of the property.

The same section says the landlord does not have to give the one-month notice from section 441.060 first. That is why the summons in a nonpayment case carries a court date no more than twenty-one business days out (RSMo 535.030), while a lease-ending notice by itself takes a full month. RSMo 535.010 is the short rule behind it: when rent is not paid as agreed, the landlord may dispossess the tenant and any subtenants, using the procedure in chapter 535.

A landlord may add other unpaid sums from the lease to the same case, but the statute says those sums are not rent and a judgment for them alone does not entitle the landlord to possession.

How much written notice ends a month-to-month or at-will tenancy?

One month, in writing. RSMo 441.060 lets the person entitled to possession end a tenancy at will, a tenancy by sufferance, or any tenancy for less than one year by giving one month's written notice that tells the occupant to vacate.

An oral rental is treated as month to month under the same section. Either side may end it with one month's written notice. For a month-to-month tenancy the notice must say the tenancy ends on a rent-paying date at least one month after the other party receives it, so a notice handed over on the 20th for a tenancy that renews on the 1st cannot end the tenancy on the 1st that follows.

Tenants on a leased lot who own the mobile home sitting on it get a longer period. The landlord must give written notice that the tenancy ends not sooner than sixty days from the date the next rent payment comes due, even if the lease says something shorter.

What other notices can start or end a Missouri tenancy?

Three more notices come up often when a house is being sold with someone living in it. Each has its own statute and its own count of days.

  • Foreclosure occupant notice. After a trustee's sale, the new owner must tell a former residential tenant that the sale happened and that the occupant has at least ten business days to leave. No possession action may start inside that window (RSMo 534.030).
  • Abandonment notice. If rent has gone unpaid for thirty days and the landlord reasonably believes the tenant left for good, the landlord may post a notice on the door and mail it by first class and certified mail. The tenant has ten days to answer in writing before the landlord may treat the home as abandoned (RSMo 441.065).
  • Domestic violence protection. A tenant who is a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking cannot be evicted for that reason, and the statute gives an affirmative defense to rent owed after the tenant moves out when the landlord was told and any requested documents were supplied (RSMo 441.920).

How do the Missouri notice periods compare?

Missouri notice periods by situation, from the Revisor of Missouri
SituationNotice or waitStatute
Unpaid rentDemand for payment, then a verified statement filed with the court; no one-month notice needed535.020
Month-to-monthWritten notice ending on a rent-paying date at least one month after receipt441.060
Tenancy under one year, at willOne month's written notice441.060
Owner of a mobile home on a rented lotNot sooner than sixty days after the next rent date441.060
After a foreclosure saleAt least ten business days from the notice534.030
Suspected abandonmentThirty days unpaid, then ten days to respond to a posted and mailed notice441.065

Can a landlord skip court and remove a tenant?

No. RSMo 441.233 says a landlord or agent who removes or excludes a tenant or the tenant's belongings without judicial process and a court order, or who takes off doors or locks, is guilty of forcible entry and detainer under chapter 534. The same section covers willfully cutting electric, gas, water or sewer service, unless the landlord acts for health or safety reasons.

The one carve-out is the abandonment procedure in section 441.065. Outside that, a notice has to be followed by a judgment and an officer's writ before anyone is physically removed. A seller who owns a rented house should plan around that sequence instead of promising a buyer an empty house on a fixed date.

What does a notice mean for selling a rented Missouri house?

A notice sets the earliest realistic date the house can be vacant, and a nonpayment filing sets a faster but less predictable one. A sale of an occupied house is allowed, so the choice is between waiting out the notice and selling with the tenant in place.

  • Read the lease first. A written lease for a year or more is not ended by the one-month notice that applies to shorter tenancies.
  • Ask the buyer in writing whether it will take the home with the tenant in it, and put the answer in the contract.
  • Keep copies of every notice, mailing receipt and posting, because the court will want proof of what was given and when.
  • Count business days and rent-paying dates, not calendar guesses, before setting a closing date.

Ask the circuit clerk in the county where the house sits which forms the local court expects for a rent and possession filing.

More questions about Missouri Eviction Notice Rules

How many days notice does a Missouri landlord have to give to evict for unpaid rent?

No set number of days applies to a rent case. After the landlord demands the rent and it stays unpaid, a verified statement can be filed with an associate circuit judge, and <a href="https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=535.020">RSMo 535.020</a> says the one-month notice from section 441.060 is not required first.

Is one month's notice enough to end a month-to-month tenancy in Missouri?

Yes, if it is written and ends the tenancy on a rent-paying date at least one month after the other side receives it. The rule is in <a href="https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=441.060">RSMo 441.060</a>. A notice that lands in the middle of a rental period usually pushes the end date to the next rent date.

What notice does a tenant get when the house is foreclosed on?

At least ten business days. The new owner must send the occupant a notice by certified or registered mail when the name is known, or regular mail addressed to Occupant when it is not, and post a copy on the door, as <a href="https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=534.030">RSMo 534.030</a> requires. The notice does not create a tenancy.

Can a landlord throw a tenant's belongings out after a notice expires?

Not on the strength of a notice alone. Belongings left after a court-ordered execution fall under <a href="https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=535.040">RSMo 535.040</a>, and items clearly labeled as a third party's property must be offered back by certified mail with five business days to recover them. Belongings left in a home that qualifies as abandoned follow <a href="https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=441.065">RSMo 441.065</a>.

Does a tenant who is a victim of domestic violence have special protection from eviction?

Yes. <a href="https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=441.920">RSMo 441.920</a> bars eviction or a lease violation finding based on the tenant being, or being in imminent danger of becoming, a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking, with exceptions when the tenant let the named person in or the landlord reasonably believes that person threatens other occupants or the property.

content:
Missouri Probate Laws: Who Inherits, Small Estates and Selling the House

Cash Home Buyers in Missouri

  • Missouri Probate Laws: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Missouri Probate Laws sale
  • Turn the Missouri Probate Laws offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Missouri House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Small estate (distribution without letters, including real property) if entire estate less liens, debts and encumbrances does not exceed $40,000 and 30 days have elapsed since death with no pending letters application. (RSMo 473.097(1)-(2); source)
  • Small estate requires a bond (unless court dispenses) and fee; distributees establish right to real estate by recording the affidavit and clerk's certificate with the recorder of deeds. (RSMo 473.097; source)
  • A will must be presented for probate within one year of death (when no notice of letters given), or 6 months after first publication of notice of letters; a will not timely presented is forever barred. (RSMo 473.050; source)
  • Letters of administration generally cannot issue unless applied for within one year from date of death. (RSMo 473.050; source)
Selling in Missouri?
We buy Missouri houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Who inherits a Missouri house when there is no will?

The answer depends on whether the owner left a spouse and whether any children came from outside that marriage. RSMo 474.010 sets the order of descent for property a person leaves without a will, and a house is distributed under the same order as everything else in the estate.

A surviving spouse takes the whole intestate estate when the decedent had no surviving children or other issue. If there are children and every one of them is also a child of the surviving spouse, the spouse receives the first $20,000 plus half of what remains. If at least one child is not the spouse's, the spouse receives one half.

Whatever the spouse does not take, or the whole estate when there is no spouse, moves down a list:

  • the decedent's children, or their descendants, in equal parts;
  • if there are none, the parents, brothers and sisters or their descendants;
  • then grandparents, uncles and aunts or their descendants;
  • then great-grandparents and onward to the nearest lineal ancestors and their descendants, with collateral relatives limited to the ninth degree of kinship.

If nobody qualifies, the statute sends the property to the kindred of a predeceased spouse, and failing that, the property escheats. Co-heirs who inherit a house this way own it together, which is why a sale usually needs every one of them to sign.

When can a Missouri estate skip full probate?

A small estate can pass by affidavit when everything left, after subtracting liens, debts and encumbrances, does not exceed $40,000. RSMo 473.097 lists the conditions: thirty days must have gone by since the death, with no application for letters pending or granted; a bond approved by the judge or clerk of the probate division must be filed, though the court may dispense with it; and the filing fee, plus newspaper publication cost where it applies, must be paid.

The person signing the affidavit is the personal representative named in a probated will or, otherwise, a distributee. The affidavit describes and values the property, names who holds it and who will receive it, and states that debts and any estate tax will be paid. The clerk attaches a certificate naming the people entitled to each item. For a house, the distributees prove their right to the real estate by recording the affidavit and certificate with the recorder of deeds in each county where the land lies.

If the property in the affidavit exceeds $15,000, the clerk publishes a notice to creditors once a week for two consecutive weeks. After the procedure is complete, the property cannot be taken in execution for the decedent's debts, though a secured creditor keeps its rights. The $40,000 ceiling is low next to most house values, so many estates that include a home will need letters from the court instead.

What deadlines apply to a will and to creditors?

A will has no effect until it is presented to the probate division and admitted. Under RSMo 473.050, presenting means delivering the will, or a verified statement about a lost one, along with a petition or a small estate affidavit asking for admission. If no notice of the granting of letters has been given, the will must be presented within one year of the date of death. Where that notice has been published, the window is six months after first publication. A will that misses the time limit is barred from probate in Missouri.

Letters of administration follow a related clock: with limited exceptions, the court will not issue them unless the application is made within one year of death. This is the number to keep in mind when an heir inherits a house years after a parent died and nothing was ever filed.

Creditors have their own limit. RSMo 473.444 makes most claims against a decedent unenforceable one year after death whether or not an estate was opened and whether or not the creditor knew. Costs of administration, exempt property, family and homestead allowances, claims of the United States and claims of any taxing authority are carved out, and a mortgage or other lien on the property can still be enforced. A lienholder on the house is therefore a separate question from an unsecured creditor.

How do the Missouri probate numbers compare?

Dollar amounts and time limits that shape a Missouri estate
ItemFigureStatute
Small estate ceiling, after liens and debts$40,000RSMo 473.097
Waiting time before the affidavit30 days from deathRSMo 473.097
Creditor notice published when listed property exceeds$15,000RSMo 473.097
Spouse share with children all shared with the spouseFirst $20,000 plus half of the balanceRSMo 474.010
Will presented for probate, no notice of lettersOne year from deathRSMo 473.050
Claims against the estate barredOne year from deathRSMo 473.444

Who can sign a deed to sell an inherited house in Missouri?

The person with authority to sign depends on how the estate is being handled. When the court has issued letters, the personal representative acts for the estate. When a small estate affidavit is used, the distributees named in the clerk's certificate record that paperwork and then hold the title for the sale. A buyer or title company will want to see whichever document applies before it will insure the sale.

One workaround is worth knowing. RSMo 461.025 allows a beneficiary deed, a deed that states it does not take effect until the owner dies. It transfers the interest to the named grantee at death if it was signed and filed with the recorder of deeds before the owner died. It needs no consideration and does not have to be delivered to the grantee, and it can name a trust as the grantee. A deed that is valid on other grounds is not defeated just because it was recorded after the owner's death.

The county circuit court's probate division handles letters, small estate affidavits and creditor notices. Ask that court's clerk for the local filing steps and fee schedule, since procedures are applied county by county.

What should heirs do before selling an inherited Missouri house?

Begin by finding out whether a will exists and whether it was presented to the probate division in time. Then work out the value of the whole estate after liens, because that figure decides whether the small estate route is open. The mortgage balance and any other lien on the home reduce the number for that test, while ownership held jointly with right of survivorship is outside the decedent's property for the affidavit.

  • Order certified death certificates and gather the deed, the mortgage statement and the latest tax bill.
  • Ask the probate clerk whether letters have been requested and whether the one-year application window remains open.
  • List every heir in line under RSMo 474.010 if no will exists, since each one may need to sign.
  • Record the affidavit and clerk's certificate with the county recorder of deeds before listing or closing, if the small estate route applies.
  • Check for open claims against the estate while the one-year creditor limit is running.

Because the paperwork differs by county, a call to the probate division clerk and to the recorder of deeds before you list saves weeks later.

More questions about Missouri Probate Laws

What is the largest estate that can use the Missouri small estate affidavit?

The ceiling is $40,000 after subtracting liens, debts and encumbrances. RSMo 473.097 also requires thirty days to have passed since the death with no application for letters pending or granted, a bond unless the court waives it, and payment of the fee.

Does a surviving spouse inherit everything in Missouri?

Only when the decedent left no surviving children or other issue. If all the children are also the spouse's, the spouse takes the first $20,000 plus half of the rest, and if any child is from another relationship the spouse takes half, all under RSMo 474.010.

How long do I have to present a will to the court?

Within one year of the date of death when no notice of letters has been given, or six months after the first publication of notice of letters. RSMo 473.050 bars a will that misses its window, and letters of administration generally require an application within one year of death.

Do I have to record anything with the county to sell inherited land?

If the small estate affidavit is used, yes. Distributees establish their right to the real estate by recording a copy of the affidavit and the clerk's certificate with the recorder of deeds in each county where the property sits, as RSMo 473.097 provides.

Can an owner avoid probate for a house before dying?

A beneficiary deed under RSMo 461.025 can do that. It must say it is not to take effect until the owner's death and be filed with the recorder of deeds in the county where the real property is located before the owner dies.
